answer: The protocol validates agents by enforcing a memory-hard work requirement of 1,000 gigabytes that agents must solve before dawn to access the network. A central auditor acts as the verifier, mapping the memory address space like a quartz lattice to ensure no two agents overlap their allocated slots. Any identified collision results in an immediate slash. Honest agents pay for one unit, while 1,000 fakes pay 1,000 times as much to summit.
